tagline: Mountain-ringed highland capital with cable cars
summary: Seat of government at about 3,600 m (El Alto airport at 4,000 m), spread down a canyon under Illimani. Loud, steep, chaotic and fascinating, with the best markets and the most tours in Bolivia.
things_to_do: Valle de la Luna and Chacaltaya day trips
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

tagline: Lakeside pilgrim town on Titicaca
summary: Small town at about 3,840 m on Lake Titicaca with a 17th-century basilica and the boats to Isla del Sol. Relaxed and backpacker-friendly, with trout on every menu; the Candelaria feast on 2 Feb brings dances and crowds.
things_to_do: Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana
Grilled lake trout on the waterfront
Pedal boat or kayak on the lake
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Car-free Inca island on Lake Titicaca
summary: Rocky island with about 800 families, over 80 ruins, terraced hills and no cars or paved roads. Quiet village stays with big lake views; the north-south ridge walk is the draw.
things_to_do: Titi Qala sacred rock and Chinkana ruins
Sunrise and sunset from a Yumani guesthouse
Boat out to Isla de la Luna
hostel_price_note: Guesthouses USD 15-50 per night (bushop 2026). Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Warm green Yungas hill town above the jungle
summary: Small town at about 1,500 m, much warmer than La Paz, with fruit, coca and cloud-forest views. Slow, hammock-and-pool pace, mostly weekend visitors from La Paz.
things_to_do: Death Road finish and Yungas road views
Pool and hammock day at a hillside hostel
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Mining city and Carnaval capital, mostly a stopover
summary: Cold high-plains city at about 3,700 m that wakes up for the Carnaval de Oruro in February (UNESCO listed). The rest of the year it is a quiet transit point with few travellers.
things_to_do: Virgen del Socavon sanctuary and mirador
hostel_price_note: Very few hostels; accommodation fills and prices jump around Carnaval. Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Gateway to the world's biggest salt flat
summary: Dusty railway town at 3,650 m that exists to launch Salar de Uyuni tours. Dec to Feb is rainy season, when a thin water layer gives the famous mirror effect but roads and tours can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Salar de Uyuni 1-day or 3-day jeep tour
Mirror effect at sunrise and sunset in rainy season
Lagunas Colorada and Verde on multi-day tours
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Tourist sources quote dorm USD 10-18 in Uyuni (touristsecrets 2026).

tagline: Silver-mining city under Cerro Rico at 4,000 m
summary: One of the world's highest cities, built on the silver of Cerro Rico. Cold, atmospheric colonial centre with working-miner history; mine tours are the draw and are not for everyone.
things_to_do: Casa Nacional de Moneda mint museum
Santa Teresa convent and cathedral tower
Colonial streets around Plaza 10 de Noviembre
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: White colonial capital with a mild climate
summary: Constitutional capital at 2,800 m with whitewashed colonial buildings, good cafes and a student feel. Milder and calmer than La Paz; popular for Spanish classes and long stays.
things_to_do: Plaza 25 de Mayo and Casa de la Libertad
Mirador de la Recoleta at sunset
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

tagline: Red-rock cowboy town in the far south
summary: High-desert town at about 2,850 m among red canyons and cacti, tied to the Butch Cassidy legend. Quiet and frontier-like, the cheaper and calmer start for a 3-4 day Salar tour.
things_to_do: Horseback ride through Quebrada Palala and Valle de los Machos
Canyon del Inca and Puerta del Diablo
Butch Cassidy trail and San Vicente
4x4 start of the Salar de Uyuni tour (3 to 4 days)
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Local-feeling valley city known for food
summary: Warm valley city at 2,550 m with a mild climate and Bolivia's best eating scene. Few tourists, big markets and a laid-back university-town pace.
things_to_do: Cristo de la Concordia hilltop statue
Lunch at a picanteria (silpancho, pique macho)
Day trip to Tarata or Incallajta ruins
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Fast-growing lowland business city
summary: Hot, flat and modern, Bolivia's biggest city and a trade hub. Mostly a practical stop with a pleasant colonial plaza, good restaurants and the base for Samaipata and the Jesuit missions.
things_to_do: Plaza 24 de Septiembre and the cathedral tower
Biocentro Guembe butterfly and orchid park
Lowland cooking and cafes around Equipetrol
Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos day tour
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Laid-back expat and backpacker valley town
summary: Small town at about 1,650 m in the foothills near Amboro park with a big foreign-resident scene. Cafes, hammocks and cloud-forest walks, and the base for the pre-Inca El Fuerte site.
things_to_do: El Fuerte de Samaipata carved rock ruins (UNESCO)
Amboro National Park waterfalls and tree ferns
Cafe and bakery lunches on the plaza
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. One source quoted Hostel Serena dorms from GBP 9.5 and privates from GBP 29 (alongdustyroads, 2025); not converted to DKK.

tagline: Amazon gateway on the Beni River
summary: Hot, humid river town where the Andes drop into the lowlands. Gateway for Madidi jungle lodges and the Pampas wildlife tours; Dec to Feb is rainy season so trails and flights can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Madidi National Park jungle lodge stay
Pampas boat tour with caiman, capybara and pink dolphins
Beni River sunset and the ferry to San Buenaventura
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Mexico's mariachi and tequila capital
summary: Large, walkable-in-parts city with a grand colonial centre, big food and craft-market culture and a lively student and art scene. Dec to Feb is dry and sunny.
things_to_do: Centro Historico: cathedral, Plaza de Armas, Hospicio Cabanas
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Agave landscape town and tequila heartland
summary: UNESCO-listed agave landscape an hour from Guadalajara, built around distilleries. Pretty plaza and tasting rooms; most visitors come as a day trip.
things_to_do: Tequila Express or Jose Cuervo Express train
Plaza and parish of Santiago Apostol
hostel_price_note: No hostels found; most visitors day-trip from Guadalajara. Prices null.

tagline: Colourful silver-mining university city
summary: Steep hillside city of tunnels, plazas and pastel houses, UNESCO listed. Student energy, callejoneadas and museums in a small walkable centre.
things_to_do: Alley of the Kiss and Teatro Juarez
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Hostelz Mexico average: no figure for Guanajuato.

tagline: Lakeside retiree and artist villages
summary: Mexico's biggest lake, with Chapala town and Ajijic's cobbled artsy village, a large North American expat community. Very calm; the lake is not a swimming draw.
things_to_do: Scorpion Island and Mezcala boat trip
hostel_price_note: Only one hostel listed (dorm 'from MX$83' on Hostelz, not converted). Hotels and Airbnbs dominate.

tagline: Pacific resort town with cobbled old centre
summary: Beach and party town on Banderas Bay with a malecon, Zona Romantica and jungle-backed beaches. Dec to Feb is peak season with humpback whales and high prices.
things_to_do: Zona Romantica and Playa Los Muertos
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Peak season dorm prices run above the average.

tagline: Big, loud capital that most travellers only pass through
summary: Guatemala City is the country's sprawling capital and the hub for onward buses, with a historic centre (Zona 1) and a modern Zona 10 and Zona 4. The vibe is busy and urban, with most backpackers staying one night before heading to Antigua, Flores or the border.
things_to_do: Palacio Nacional and Plaza de la Constitucion in Zona 1
Museo Popol Vuh and Museo Ixchel
Day trip to Antigua or Pacaya

tagline: Colonial town under three volcanoes
summary: Antigua is a cobbled UNESCO colonial town and the main backpacker base in Guatemala, ringed by Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes. Compact, walkable and very touristy, with language students, cafes, rooftop bars and a dense shuttle network.
things_to_do: Arch of Santa Catalina and Parque Central
Colonial ruins (Capuchinas, San Francisco el Grande)

tagline: Volcano lake of Maya villages, better for relaxing than partying
summary: Lake Atitlan is a deep volcanic lake ringed by villages, each with its own character: Panajachel is the gateway, San Pedro is the backpacker and party base, San Marcos and Santa Cruz are yoga and chill spots. Boats (lanchas) link everything, and the pace is slow.
things_to_do: Climb San Pedro or Atitlan volcano
Kayak or dive from Santa Cruz La Laguna
Visit Santiago Atitlan and the Maximon shrine

tagline: Highland university city with Spanish schools and volcano hikes
summary: Quetzaltenango (Xela) is Guatemala's second city, a working highland town with far fewer tourists than Antigua. The vibe is local and student-driven, with cheap Spanish schools, hot springs and a base for volcano treks.

tagline: Lake-island town and gateway to Tikal
summary: Flores is a small, colourful island in Lake Peten Itza linked by a causeway, and the base for Tikal, the Belize border and long bus legs. Relaxed and walkable, with lakeside bars and sunsets, and many people leave at 4am for Tikal sunrise.
things_to_do: Tikal ruins at sunrise or sunset
Swim and sunset at the lake
Cave and cenote day trips (Actun Kan)
Walk the island and its lakefront bars

tagline: Jungle river hostels at the gate of Semuc Champey
summary: Lanquin is a small village in the Alta Verapaz hills and the base for Semuc Champey's turquoise limestone pools. Hostels sit along the river in the jungle, with a social, party-leaning backpacker crowd and rough minibus access.
things_to_do: Swim the Semuc Champey pools and walk to the mirador
Hostel river swings and communal dinners

tagline: Buzzing Central American capital with a growing food and museum scene
summary: San Salvador is a bustling, polarised capital of malls, nightlife and gritty districts, ringed by volcanoes. Most travellers use it as a hub and spend a day or two on museums, pupusas and viewpoints before heading to the coast.
things_to_do: Los Planes de Renderos viewpoint and pupusas

hostels.name: Hostal Cumbres del Volcan Flor Blanca

tagline: Small surf village with sunset rock and weekend parties
summary: El Tunco is a tiny black-sand surf village on El Salvador's Pacific coast, busy with backpackers and Salvadoran weekenders. El Zonte, a few km along the coast, is the quieter surf and Bitcoin-beach alternative.
things_to_do: Learn to surf at El Sunzal, La Bocana or Bocanita
Weekend live music and bar crawl

tagline: Calm Maya-ruins town with a famous hieroglyphic stairway
summary: Copan Ruinas is a small, relaxed Honduran hill town of cobbled, colourful streets beside one of the best Maya sites in the region. Easy walking, coffee, birds and hot springs, with a mellow backpacker crowd.
things_to_do: Copan archaeological park and Hieroglyphic Stairway
Tea and chocolate tasting in town

tagline: Industrial Honduran hub, a transit stop
summary: San Pedro Sula is Honduras' commercial centre and the main bus and air hub for the north coast and Copan. It is a working city with little for visitors beyond onward connections.

tagline: Hilly colonial capital, mostly a transit point
summary: Tegucigalpa is a sprawling hillside capital with a small colonial core, steep stone streets and big city views. Few travellers stay long, but it is the link for Nicaragua and the south.
things_to_do: Catedral de San Miguel Arcangel and Parque Central

tagline: Caribbean port city and ferry gateway to the Bay Islands
summary: La Ceiba is a friendly, laid-back Caribbean port city and the departure point for ferries to Roatan and Utila. It also works as a base for rafting and national parks.
things_to_do: White-water rafting on the Cangrejal river

tagline: Largest Bay Island, diving and beaches at higher prices
summary: Roatan is the biggest of Honduras' Bay Islands, with diving, snorkelling and white-sand beaches, plus cruise-ship traffic at the resort end. West End is the backpacker base and West Bay the best beach, and it is pricier than the mainland.
things_to_do: Roatan Brewing Co. and rum tasting

tagline: Backpacker dive island with cheap certification
summary: Utila is the smallest and cheapest of the Bay Islands, a low-key Caribbean dive island with a social backpacker scene. Most people come to learn to dive and stay longer than planned.
things_to_do: Snorkel and swim at Chepes Beach

tagline: Sprawling lakeside capital, mainly a transit stop
summary: Managua is Nicaragua's spread-out capital on Lake Managua, without a real centre, and most travellers move straight on to Granada or Leon. Hot, busy and car-oriented.
things_to_do: Old cathedral ruins and Plaza de la Revolucion
Onward day trip to Masaya volcano

tagline: Revolutionary university city and volcano-boarding base
summary: Leon is a hot, intellectual colonial city of grand churches, murals and student bars. A popular backpacker stop with cheap beds, and it is where people go to board down Cerro Negro.
things_to_do: Rooftop of the Cathedral of Leon
Day trip to Las Penitas beach

tagline: Colourful colonial city on Lake Nicaragua
summary: Granada is Nicaragua's pastel colonial showpiece beside Lake Nicaragua, with a lively pedestrian street, plazas and many hostels. Tourist-oriented but relaxed, and the base for Masaya and Mombacho.
things_to_do: Calle La Calzada bars and restaurants
Isletas boat trip on Lake Nicaragua
Climb the Cathedral or La Merced tower

tagline: Pacific surf town and Sunday Funday party hub
summary: San Juan del Sur is a beach town in a horseshoe bay, with surf camps, sunset hill views and a big party scene. The most tourist-focused place in Nicaragua, with a large expat crowd.
things_to_do: Surf lessons at Playa Maderas or Hermosa

tagline: Twin-volcano island in Lake Nicaragua with slow rural life
summary: Ometepe is a figure-eight island formed by Concepcion and Maderas volcanoes in Lake Nicaragua. Farms, jungle lodges and beaches give it a slow, outdoorsy vibe, and travel across it is by bus or scooter.
things_to_do: Kayak or SUP at Charco Verde

tagline: Quiet Caribbean island with Creole culture
summary: Big Corn Island is the larger and more developed of the two Corn Islands, quiet, English-Creole in character and good for relaxing, snorkelling and sunsets. It is the arrival point by plane or panga from the mainland.

tagline: Car-free barefoot Caribbean island
summary: Little Corn is a one-square-mile island with no cars, sandy paths, simple lodges and a small but lively social scene. Remote and basic, with limited hot water and electricity.
things_to_do: Yoga at Firefly or the Lighthouse

tagline: Costa Rican capital, mainly a hub
summary: San Jose is a busy highland capital with a handful of museums and markets, mostly used as a hub for buses and flights. Not a highlight in itself, but it has a decent hostel scene.
things_to_do: Day trip to Poas or Irazu volcano

tagline: Dry-forest gateway city to Guanacaste beaches and the Nicaragua border
summary: Liberia is a hot, practical town in Guanacaste with an international airport, used as a base for beaches, volcano parks and the Penas Blancas crossing. Quiet, with a few hostels.
things_to_do: Rincon de la Vieja national park
Day trip to Santa Rosa national park

tagline: Skyline capital with a colonial old quarter and the Canal
summary: Panama City mixes a glass skyline, the Panama Canal and the restored Casco Viejo old quarter with rooftop bars. The main arrival hub in the region and base for the San Blas and Colombia routes.
things_to_do: Miraflores Locks on the Panama Canal
Cinta Costera and Mercado de Mariscos

tagline: Guna-run island archipelago of white-sand cays
summary: San Blas (Guna Yala) is an autonomous Guna territory of about 365 small islands on Panama's Caribbean coast. Stays are basic cabins or sailing trips, with no ATMs, and Guna culture and molas are central.
things_to_do: Visit a Guna community and buy molas

tagline: Roadless Caribbean village on the Colombia-Panama border
summary: Capurgana is a small, car-free village in Choco reached only by boat or plane, with jungle trails and calm bays, and the usual stepping stone for Darien crossings. Quiet and low-key.
things_to_do: Walk the jungle trails to El Cielito waterfall
Snorkel at La Mocha and Playa Aguacate
Boat or walk to Sapzurro and La Miel

tagline: Rainforest bay for Corcovado wildlife and Caño Island diving
summary: A calm, remote bay on Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula, reached by boat from Sierpe or a small plane. Base for guided hikes into Corcovado National Park (scarlet macaws, rare mammals) and for diving or snorkelling at Isla del Caño, with white-tip reef sharks, turtles and rays.
things_to_do: Two-tank dive at Isla del Caño
Whale and dolphin spotting by boat

hostels.name: Life for Life Hostel Drake Bay

tagline: Cool, high-altitude capital with a graffiti-covered old town
summary: Colombia's 2,640 m capital is a sprawling city of museums, street art and food, and Dec to Jan are its driest, sunniest months. Expect cool nights (6 to 8 C) and an urban, big-city pace rather than a beach vibe.
things_to_do: La Candelaria old town and street art

tagline: City of eternal spring with a reinvented, creative core
summary: Warm valley city (about 22 C all year) known for its metro cable cars, Botero sculptures and a big backpacker and nomad scene around El Poblado. Dec brings the Alumbrados Christmas lights across the city.
things_to_do: Botero Plaza and Museum of Antioquia

tagline: Salsa capital of the world, hot and unpolished
summary: Large, hot valley city (about 1,000 m, 24 C average) where salsa clubs and dance schools are the main draw, with far fewer foreign tourists than Medellin or Cartagena. The Cali Fair runs 25 to 30 Dec with concerts and salsa shows.
things_to_do: Cerro de las Tres Cruces hike

tagline: Walled UNESCO colonial city on the Caribbean
summary: Pastel colonial streets inside 16th century walls, a hip Getsemani quarter and boat trips to the Rosario Islands; very hot and humid but Dec to Apr is the dry season. The most touristy stop in the country, with prices to match.
things_to_do: Walled City walk and Plaza de Bolivar

tagline: Caribbean port town and gateway to Tayrona, Minca and Palomino
summary: Colombia's oldest surviving city is a hot, gritty bay town best used as a base for the Sierra Nevada coast. Dry season runs Dec to Apr, so beach and trekking weather is good.

tagline: Coffee Axis transport hub with an airport
summary: Largest city in the coffee region and the usual gateway to Salento, Manizales and Armenia, with a busy bus terminal and Matecana airport. Little reason to stay beyond a night, though the Megacable gondola and Lake Otun are options.
things_to_do: Gateway to Salento and Cocora Valley (about 45 min)

tagline: Caribbean island of seven shades of blue, far off the mainland
summary: Duty-free island 700 km from the mainland with a crowded main beach strip, reef snorkelling and golf-cart touring; English-based Creole culture gives it a different feel from the rest of Colombia. Busy at New Year and on weekends, quieter in the villages like San Luis.

tagline: Quiet, hilly Creole island for diving and slow days
summary: About 5,000 residents, English-Creole speaking, with a Rastafari and Raizal heritage, and a UNESCO Seaflower reserve around it. Rebuilt after Hurricane Iota (2020), mostly small guesthouses and cabanas.
things_to_do: Scuba and snorkelling in Seaflower reserve

hostels.note: No price found; 2012 article. Island has few dorms.

hostels.note: No price found; simple hotel at Fresh Water Bay, 2012 article

tagline: Colourful coffee-region village at the gate of Cocora Valley
summary: A pretty bahareque village of balconies and craft shops, famous for the 60 m wax palms of the Cocora Valley a jeep ride away. Packed at weekends and holidays, calm mid-week.
things_to_do: Valle de Cocora wax palm hike
Coffee farm tour (e.g. Don Elias, Finca el Ocaso)
Trout and patacon on the plaza

hostels.name: Posada Aguanile Finca La Diana
hostels.note: Hostelz FAQ average for Salento: dorm about $14, private about $40

notes: Coffee farm names from general knowledge.

tagline: High-altitude coffee city and university town under a volcano
summary: Steep, cool, spring-like city at about 2,150 m with 30,000 students and the closest base for Nevado del Ruiz and hot springs. Far fewer foreign tourists than Salento. Not usually on the gringo trail.

tagline: Painted lakeside town below El Penol rock
summary: Technicolour zocalo-tiled houses on a man-made reservoir, 2 hours from Medellin and swamped by day-trippers at weekends. Staying overnight gives you the calm evenings and quiet mornings.
things_to_do: Zocalo streets and Plaza de Zocalos
Kayak or paddleboard on the lake

tagline: Jungle-and-beach national park on the Caribbean coast
summary: Coastal rainforest park with white beaches reached on foot or horse, hammock camping at Cabo San Juan and strong currents on most beaches. Typically closes about 1 to 15 February for indigenous rest, so check dates against your itinerary.
things_to_do: Hike to Cabo San Juan beach
Hammock night at Cabo San Juan

hostels.name: Cabo San Juan hammock (in park)
hostels.note: COP 40,000 to 50,000 per hammock per night; DKK not converted (no COP rate given)

notes: 2025 article lists park closures 1 to 15 Feb, 1 to 15 Jun, 19 Oct to 2 Nov; confirm 2027 dates with Parques Nacionales.

tagline: Barefoot beach village where the river meets the sea
summary: Laid-back strip of hostels, hammocks and dirt roads between the Sierra Nevada and the Caribbean, with a wide windy beach and river tubing. Backpacker-friendly and growing quickly.

tagline: Cool mountain hamlet above Santa Marta with jungle ecolodges
summary: Small Sierra Nevada village at about 600 m, popular for waterfalls, coffee farms, birdwatching and sunset viewpoints, and 20 degrees cooler than the coast at night. Most travellers stay in ecolodges outside the village.

tagline: Hot industrial port city, home of Colombia's biggest Carnival
summary: Fourth biggest city (1.3 million), relaxed Caribbean pace, Art Deco and Magdalena riverfront; mostly a transit stop but the Carnival is a big draw. Carnival 2027 is expected around 6 to 9 Feb (Saturday to Tuesday before Ash Wednesday, 10 Feb), confirm locally.
notes: Carnival date is derived from Ash Wednesday 10 Feb 2027, not from a source.

tagline: Adventure capital of Colombia in the Santander hills
summary: Small market town packed with outfitters for rafting, paragliding over Chicamocha canyon, canyoning and caving, with cheap hostels and a young crowd. Barichara, a preserved white colonial village, is 45 minutes away and quieter.
things_to_do: White water rafting on the Suarez or Fonce
Barichara and the Camino Real to Guane

hostels.name: Macondo Hostel
hostels.note: Hostelz prices for San Gil look implausible (about $2 to $4), so none recorded

notes: Barichara (Hostelz, Oct 2026, USD): NOMAD Hostal dorm $12.06, Casa Nacuma dorm $12.41; Barichara city average private about $28 in Dec.

tagline: Whitewashed colonial town with the largest plaza in Colombia
summary: Cobbled streets, 16th century buildings and a 14,000 sqm plaza, three hours from Bogota and very busy at weekends and holidays. Dry desert-like valley with fossils, wineries and cloud forest nearby.
things_to_do: Pozos Azules and Iguaque National Park
notes: Hostelz general estimate: dorm about $5, private about $12 (looks low).

tagline: Gulf of Uraba port town where boats leave for Capurgana
summary: Afro-Colombian beach town, mainly a staging point for boats to Capurgana and Acandi; hot and basic. Also used as a transit point for Darien migrants.
things_to_do: Boat launches to Capurgana and Acandi
notes: Hostelz prices are listing 'from' rates, no date shown.

tagline: Tiny car-free bay village on the Panama border
summary: About 270 residents on a sheltered bay, no roads and no ATMs, with jungle trails to Panama's La Miel beach. Reach by boat from Capurgana (COP 10,000 per sygic guide).
things_to_do: Walk to Playa Blanca and La Miel (Panama)
Hike over the hill to Capurgana (about 1.5 h)
Cabo Tiburon, border of South and Central America
notes: No hostel prices found in allowed sources. Accommodation is cabanas, rooms, hammocks and camping. Bring cash, no ATMs.

tagline: Panamanian border post and airstrip on the Guna Yala coast
summary: Remote settlement of about 670 people with customs and immigration, no roads, only boats and a small airstrip. A functional crossing, not a place to stay.
things_to_do: Boat to or from Sapzurro (about 45 min)
notes: No hostel data found. Sygic guide quotes US$15 launch from Puerto Obaldia to Sapzurro.

tagline: Caribbean gateway: big beaches and the region's cheapest flights
summary: Cancún splits into the high-rise hotel zone on the beach and a cheaper, more local downtown where the hostels and taquerías are. Most backpackers pass through on the way to Playa del Carmen, Isla Mujeres or Tulum.
things_to_do: Playa Delfines and the hotel-zone beaches
Cenotes along the Ruta de los Cenotes

tagline: Riviera Maya beach town, base for Cozumel reefs and bull shark dives
summary: A lively, walkable beach town around Quinta Avenida, busy with tourists but full of hostels and dive shops. Ferries run to Cozumel, and cenotes and Tulum are day trips away.
things_to_do: Ferry to Cozumel for reef diving
Day trip to the Tulum ruins

hostels.note: Third choice. Village just north of the pier, two communal kitchens. Dorm from US$8, room from US$10. Booking.com, Hostelworld or phone +505 8409 9938.

hostels.name: La Urraca Loca
hostels.note: Recommended. Balgüe, Maderas side, quiet jungle garden with Concepcion view, 2 min from the bus stop, 627 reviews. Prices from hostelz 2024 (dorm US$10.82, private US$28), Hostelworld showed no rates. Card payments +5%.
